title: Cut the AER off at a chosen hour - the original timing experiment
mechanism: The AER is a physical strip of thickened ectoderm at the distal tip of the bud. Excising it stops distal outgrowth from that moment, and what is already specified proximally still forms. The level of the resulting truncation is therefore a function of WHEN the ridge is removed, which makes this the oldest and most direct demonstration that limb loss is a timing problem rather than only a genetic one.
intervention: Microsurgical excision of the AER from a chick limb bud at a staged time point. In mouse this is not practical in utero; the equivalents are the genetic routes (gene-aer-fgf4-fgf8) or explant culture (invitro-limb-bud-explant).
predicted_phenotype: Progressive distal truncation whose level tracks the stage of excision: earlier removal leaves less limb. The classical series is quantitative.

evidence.cite: Summerbell D 1974, J Embryol Exp Morphol 32:651-60, 'A quantitative analysis of the effect of excision of the AER from the chick limb-bud'
evidence.finding: PubMed record retrieved and the title and MeSH terms (Ectoderm, Extremities, Gestational Age, Humerus, Radius, Ulna, Morphogenesis, Wings) confirm a staged quantitative excision series in chick. NO ABSTRACT IS AVAILABLE in the PubMed record, so we have not read any result statement from this paper and we report only what the record itself shows.

evidence.cite: Lewandoski M, Sun X & Martin GR 2000, Nat Genet 26:460-3
evidence.finding: States the classical premise independently: 'Removal of the AER in chick results in limbs lacking distal skeletal elements' and FGF proteins can substitute for the AER.

reversibility: Not reversible once cut, but FGF protein beads substitute for the removed ridge, which is the sufficiency half of the experiment and makes the manipulation effectively two-way in chick.
lethality_risk: Low in chick; the manipulation is local.
specificity: One limb, one bud, at one time - the most spatially and temporally precise intervention available anywhere in this design space.
difficulty: low in chick (a classical embryology technique), impractical in mouse in utero.
what_we_would_run: This is the physical ground truth for the timing axis. Our growth simulators can reproduce 'stop distal outgrowth at time t and see what is already specified', and the chick excision series is the only dataset that could calibrate such a model - except that we cannot read Summerbell's numbers from the PubMed record, so the calibration is not available to us today.
open_questions: We could not access the numerical series. Any claim we make about the quantitative relationship between excision stage and truncation level would be unsupported by what we actually read.

title: Kill the AER genetically with a cell-autonomous toxin
mechanism: Instead of cutting the ridge off, express diphtheria toxin A under a promoter active in AER precursors, so the signalling centre is deleted cell-autonomously and without surgery. This is the standard technique for ablating an organiser in the mouse; it has been used to remove the roof plate from the neural tube and to ablate lens precursors before placode formation, both of which produced the expected loss of the structures that depended on the organiser.
intervention: An AER-restricted promoter (for example an Msx2 or limb-ectoderm element) driving attenuated DTA, or a Cre driver crossed to a ROSA26-LoxP-DTA reporter.
predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED, NOT OBSERVED. By analogy with AER excision the expectation is distal truncation set by the onset of toxin expression, with the proximal skeleton retained. We found NO published AER DTA ablation in our searches and we would not state a phenotype for it.

evidence.cite: Lee KJ, Dietrich P & Jessell TM 2000, Nature 403:734-40, 'Genetic ablation reveals that the roof plate is essential for dorsal interneuron specification'
evidence.finding: A genetic strategy selectively ablated the roof plate in mouse embryos; embryos without a roof plate lack all the interneuron subtypes normally generated in the dorsal third of the neural tube, from loss of non-autonomous signals. Establishes the method for organiser ablation in mouse.

evidence.cite: Zhang Y et al. 2008, Dev Biol 323:53-63, 'Dominant inhibition of lens placode formation in mice'
evidence.finding: Transgenic mice expressing attenuated diphtheria toxin (Tox176) from a modified Pax6 promoter ablated lens precursor cells BEFORE placode formation, allowing the role of the structure to be tested at its earliest stage. Demonstrates that pre-placodal ablation with an attenuated toxin is achievable.

reversibility: None - toxin-killed cells do not return. The control is over WHEN, not whether.
lethality_risk: Depends entirely on promoter leakiness; an attenuated toxin is used precisely to keep ablation local.
specificity: As specific as the promoter. An AER-only driver would be the most limb-specific cellular intervention possible.
difficulty: medium-high, and the honest difficulty is finding a driver that is on in AER precursors and nowhere that matters.
what_we_would_run: Nothing. This route is on the page as a clearly-labelled PROPOSAL, to show the shape of the design space rather than to claim a result. Presenting it as established would be the exact failure mode the page exists to avoid.
open_questions: Does an AER-specific driver with the right onset exist? Our search covered 'diphtheria toxin ablation apical ectodermal ridge genetic mouse' on PubMed and returned four records, none of them an AER ablation. That is the scope of our negative, not a statement about the literature.

title: Remove the ZPA's signal at a chosen stage - digits disappear in a defined order
mechanism: SHH from the ZPA does two separable jobs: a very transient early patterning job that assigns digit identity, and an extended growth-promoting job during which the digit precursor mesenchyme expands and is recruited into condensing digit primordia. Deleting Shh progressively earlier with an inducible Cre removes progressively more digits, and the order in which they are lost mirrors an alternating anterior-posterior sequence of normal digit formation.
intervention: Tamoxifen-inducible Cre (ShhCreER) with a conditional Shh allele, dosed at a chosen embryonic day.
predicted_phenotype: Progressive loss of digits, with the number lost set by how early Shh is removed. Not limb loss: the stylopod and zeugopod are not the target. This route tunes AUTOPOD CONTENT, precisely and reproducibly.

evidence.cite: Zhu J et al. 2008, Dev Cell 14:624-32, 'Uncoupling Sonic hedgehog control of pattern and expansion of the developing limb bud'
evidence.finding: 'Deleting the mouse Shh gene at different times using a conditional Cre line, we find that Shh functions to control limb development in two phases: a very transient, early patterning phase regulating digit identity, and an extended growth-promoting phase ... The progressive loss of digits upon successively earlier Shh removal mirrors this alternating sequence.'

evidence.cite: Scherz PJ et al. 2004, Science 305:396-9, 'The limb bud Shh-Fgf feedback loop is terminated by expansion of former ZPA cells'
evidence.finding: Shh-expressing cells and their descendants cannot express Gremlin; their proliferation forms a physical barrier separating the Shh signal from Gremlin-expressing cells, which breaks the Shh-Fgf4 loop and thereby affects limb size.

reversibility: Reversible in the sense that matters for experimental design: the lesion is applied at a time of the experimenter's choosing, not at fertilisation. It is not reversible after the fact.
lethality_risk: Low when induction is late enough to miss the early Shh requirements in notochord and neural tube - which is exactly the advantage of the inducible allele over the germline null (compare gene-shh-gli3, which is catastrophic).
difficulty: low-medium; the alleles are published and tamoxifen dosing is routine.
what_we_would_run: This is the best-posed quantitative dataset in the whole design space for our Lean threshold work: an ordered stimulus (induction time) mapping to an ordered, countable outcome (digit number). Stating 'given a monotone map from signal duration to element count, an ordered duration series implies an ordered count series', then mutating the monotonicity and the threshold and showing Lean rejects both mutants, is a bounded job. It proves our reasoning is consistent; it proves nothing about mice, and the page must say that in the same sentence.
open_questions: Scherz et al. make loop termination a consequence of CELL LINEAGE geometry rather than of a transcriptional timer. A model with no spatial representation of former-ZPA descendants cannot express that mechanism at all.

title: Tune the limb by changing how fast the morphogen falls apart
mechanism: FGF10 is an intrinsically unstable protein that unfolds and is rapidly inactivated at 37 C, and the thermodynamic stability of the 22 mammalian FGFs varies widely. Engineered FGF10 variants with a melting temperature more than 19 C above wild type bind receptors, activate signalling and induce gene expression identically in cell assays, yet behave completely differently in tissue - which implies that protein half-life, not receptor affinity, is part of how the limb reads this signal.
intervention: Knock in a stabilised (or, for limb reduction, a destabilised) Fgf10 allele. Stabilised FGF10 variants implanted into chicken limb buds markedly altered limb morphogenesis and inhibited growth of mouse embryonic tibias.
predicted_phenotype: Stabilised direction (measured): suppressed lung branching with increased alveolarisation and epithelial expansion; inhibited embryonic tibia growth; markedly altered limb morphogenesis in chick bud implants. Destabilised direction (PROPOSED, not measured): a graded hypomorphic FGF10 signal, predicted to give partial limb reduction rather than the all-or-nothing amelia of the null.

evidence.cite: Czyrek AA et al. 2025, Cell Mol Life Sci 82:167, 'Increased thermal stability of FGF10 leads to ectopic signaling during development'
evidence.finding: 'FGF10, an important limb and lung morphogen, exists as an intrinsically unstable protein that is prone to unfolding and is rapidly inactivated at 37 C'; STAB variants with +19 C melting temperature were indistinguishable in receptor binding and signalling in cells but 'inhibited the growth of mouse embryonic tibias and markedly altered limb morphogenesis when implanted into chicken limb buds, collectively demonstrating that thermal instability should be considered an important regulator of FGF function that prevents ectopic signaling'.

reversibility: A knock-in allele is not reversible; but recombinant protein delivery is, and the published work is a bead/implant experiment, which is the acute, dose-controlled version.
lethality_risk: Unknown for a destabilised germline allele. If it behaves as a graded Fgf10 hypomorph the lung phenotype scales with it, so the lethality that sinks the Fgf10 null is likely to scale too.
specificity: Poor at the gene level (FGF10 serves many organs) but unusual at the BIOPHYSICAL level: nothing else on this page proposes to tune a phenotype by changing a protein's folding stability rather than its sequence-level function.
difficulty: high, and genuinely novel - we found no published destabilised-FGF10 animal.
what_we_would_run: This is the one route where a protein-structure model, rather than a genome model, is the right tool: predict melting temperature for designed FGF10 variants and check against the measured STAB series, which gives a held-out numerical benchmark with real values. We have not run it and have no structure pipeline today.
open_questions: Does a destabilised FGF10 produce a graded limb phenotype, or does the limb buffer ligand half-life entirely? Unknown; the published direction is the stabilising one.
